title: Compliance Milestone Tracker: Cross-Org SSO Cutover Plan with Audit Log Retention SLAs
creator: Elena Martínez
description:
Objective: Define and execute a milestone-driven plan to cut over customers to org-level SSO (SAML) while simultaneously enforcing updated audit-log retention SLAs required for SOC2/ISO evidence. This ticket tracks cross-functional milestones, acceptance criteria, and the evidence automation required to sign off compliance gates.

Scope: (a) Migration playbook and runbooks for SSO cutover (pilot -> staged rollout -> org-wide), (b) Audit log retention policy implementation (7/30/90-day buckets + export/archival automation), (c) Evidence capture for SOC2/ISO (proof of migration, change approvals, audit log snapshots), (d) Console UI indicators and Alerts for customers and internal auditors.

Out of scope: Re-architecting logging backend; deep infra changes outside ENG-22110 patch set (tracked as dependency).
acceptance_criteria: Pilot cohort (5 customers) successfully migrated using the playbook with <2% auth failure rate
Audit logs for migrated orgs retained and queryable for 90 days per policy without manual intervention
Evidence bundle generation script produces auditor-ready artifacts (signed hashes, OFA) for 100% of migration events
Console shows SSO status and retention SLA per org; internal compliance dashboard reflects retention parity with policy
success_metrics: Pilot success rate >= 95% within pilot window
Migration-induced support tickets <= 0.5 tickets per migrated org in 14 days
Automated audit evidence completeness >= 98% as measured by evaluation harness
Time-to-evidence generation <= 10 minutes after migration completion
decisions: Use staged rollout: Pilot (5 orgs) -> Canary (20 orgs) -> Bulk migration
Adopt current logging retention buckets (7/30/90) and implement export to S3 for archival rather than increasing DB retention
Evidence artefact format: zip of JSON snapshots + signed SHA256 manifest to satisfy auditor immutability requirements
open_questions: Do we require per-customer KMS-wrapped audit archives for customers with 'legal hold'? (Asked to Security)
Can Dedicated customers be added to the pilot or do network constraints block SSO changes?
Is the customer consent UX for forced SSO migration acceptable under current privacy policy?
comments: 2025-02-19 - Kickoff: cross-functional kickoff with Eng, Security, CS. Agreed pilot scope and success metrics. Action: ENG to evaluate retention impact (Marcus)

2025-03-03 - Security review: Priya: KMS per-customer optional; flagged legal-hold as high risk. Action: capture legal-hold as a metadata flag in evidence bundle
2025-03-07 - Engineering update: ENG-22110 patch reduces log write latency by 18% but requires migration window change. Proposed migration window moved to 02:00-05:00 PT for minimal traffic
2025-03-10 - Blocker noted: Some Dedicated customers use legacy SAML endpoints that need partner coordination. Action: CS to schedule partner calls (Aaron)
2025-03-12 - Plan update: Added canary stage (20 orgs) after pilot. Updated runbook to include rollback steps and automated evidence snapshot after each rollback. Assigned tasks in Cycle 2025-W08
notes: Trade-offs: opting for S3 export keeps DB costs predictable but requires secure key management for archives. We chose this to avoid long-tail DB storage growth.
Implementation approach: incremental migration helpers (token exchange + phased metadata flip) to avoid wide blast radius. Keep per-org feature-flag for immediate rollback.
Monitoring: create a Pulse alert for auth errors >1% over 15m during migration windows; add a retention drift job that reports by org weekly
